findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the hand sink int he kitchen was observed to be coming off. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the hand sink will be caulked to the wall properly. Ensure that the hand sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed pork being stored over cooked breaded shrimp and raw veggies in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC and PIC removed to raw pork to be stored properly. Ensure that appropriate storage order is observed to avoid cross contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: A scoop with a dirty handle was observed lying sideways in the sugar storage container. Discuss with PIC and the scoop was taken out to be cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are routinely monitored and cleaned to avoid contamination of food items. [Pf]
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: A bowl was observed containing shrimp in water thawing in the walk in refrigerator. Discuss with PIC and the thawing method was corrected. The Shrimp was received frozen and was put in the bowl of water and placed in the refrigerator to be thawed. Ensure that the adequate thawing methods are used for food items. [C]
findings.citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soils. 
1. The exterior of the storage containers in the dry storage appeared to have an accumulation of soils. 
2. The accumulation of grease was observed on the top of the shelving on the grill.
3. The rice cooker table next to the fryer was observed to have an accumulation of grease build up on the sides and underneath.
4. The accumulation of ice buildup was observed in the sitting freezer at the entrance of the walk-in fridge.
Discuss with PIC and PIC noted that the above mentioned areas would be cleaned. Ensure that equipments in a facility are routinely monitored and cleaned to avoid the accumulation of soils. Make sure that food contact surfaces and non-food contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. [C]

6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

One of the sugar storage containers was observed broken. Discussed with PIC and the container will be replaced. Ensure that storage containers are continuously checked for possible repairs.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following areas were observed to have an accumulation of soils/debris:
-The phone used to take call in orders had an accumulation of food debris. 
-The bottom of the right stand up freezer is observed with food debris. 
-The ledge of the chest freezer is observed with food debris. 
Ensure these areas are cleaned to remove the current accumulation of food debris and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The shelf next to the fryer is observed to have an accumulation of grease on its surface. The PIC was made aware of this shelf and will be cleaning and sanitizing this shelf before continuing to use it. Ensure that all surfaces of equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The left white standing freezer is observed to have an accumulation of food debris on the bottom shelf and is need of cleaning. Facility PIC stated they clean it every other week. Due to the nature of some of the foods having debris that falls off easily, practices are being changed to cleaning the bottom of the freezer every week. Ensure cleaning takes place at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.  
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The phone available for use in the kitchen is observed to have an excessive accumulation of food/soil debris. This phone is currently covered in what appears to be plastic wrap. The old covering needs to be removed and replaced with a new cover and then this cover needs to be replaced at a frequency necessary to maintain the phone clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The floor behind the right standing freezer and the dry storage shelving are observed to have an accumulation of soil/debris. These pieces of equipment need to be pulled away from the wall on a regular basis and these surfaces need to be cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: In the prep cooler it was observed that a tub was sitting on top of the other vegetables with the bottom of the tub in contact with the food items in the cooler. The tub was removed form this location and placed in a manner that prevented contamination during storage. Ensure that the food items are protected from contamination during storage, preparation, and display.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: The back door to the facility is observed to be in a state of disrepair with visible gaps in the door frame and holes in the screen. This entry point will need to be repaired with a new screen and the door will need to be repaired in a manner that protects the establishment form the entry of insects and rodents. 
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The handles of the white standing freezers are observed to have an accumulation of food debris/soil. Ensure these handles and the surfaces of the freezers are cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of food debris/soil residues.
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The floor behind the white standing freezers and the floor behind the white chest freezer is observed to have an accumulation of soil/debris. These pieces of equipment need to be pulled away from the wall on a regular basis and these surfaces need to be cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
The floor under the cook-line is also observed to have an accumulation of soil/food debris. Ensure the cook-line floor is clenaed and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: There were two knives observed to be stored between the wall and a metal pipe. These knives were removed and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle before being used again. THere was one knife also observed to be stored in between the prep table and the prep cooler. This knife was also removed and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that knives and other equipment are stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket int he kitchen was tested and recorded at <10ppm chlorine. More bleach was added to the solution. The solution was tested again and recorded at 100ppm chlorine. Ensure test strips are used throughout the day and that the chemical sanitizer is at least 100ppm chlorine to allow the sanitizer to perform its duties.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: There were two knives observed to be stored between the wall and a metal pipe. These knives were removed and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle before being used again. Ensure that knives and other equipment are stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Raw chicken was observed to be stored above frozen beef in the white freezer. Education was provided to the facility that even though it is a freezer, proper storage needs to be used based on cooking temperatures for reasons associated with cross contamination possibilities. Ensure proepr storage practices take place for all food items int he kitchen.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Wiping cloths were observed stored outside of the sanitizer bucket on various surfaces in the facility. These wiping cloths were placed into the sanitizer solution during th inspection Andy will remain in the sanitizer between uses.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: Scoops with no handles were observed to be used to portion out sugar and other powders in the dry storage area. These scoops were removed from service and replaced with scoops containing handles. ENsure this practice continues to better protect the food items form contamination during storage and use.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 1) Handles to coolers are sticky and the front reach in cooler/freezer has visible soil on the handles. Clean handles to coolers. 2) Make sure to clean and sanitize three compartment sink before doing dishes as it is soiled with food debris at the time of the inspection. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: 1) Observed par-cooked chicken cooling in a perforated bowl that was sitting on top of cardboard egg crates. It was discussed that the cardboard could be contaminated from the raw shell eggs and should not be used in contact with ready to eat foods. Use something that is smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable. 2) Observed shell eggs stored above carrots in the walk in cooler. Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products as carrots have a lower cooking temperature than shell eggs and must be stored in proper order to prevent contamination. 3-302.11  (P)   Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed in use knife being stored in the space between the edge of the prep cooler and the adjacent prep table--this area is soiled with debris accumulation. Store in use utensils in clean, sanitized areas or clean and sanitize these areas at least every 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
1) Observed lemon scented bleach being used as a sanitizer. Bleach when used as a sanitizer must be plain bleach, and under the FDA food code it must have an EPA registration number and instructions for use on food contact surfaces on the label. Provide approved bleach. 
2) Observed a soy sauce bucket containing a white powder substance and a chemical sprayer, reported to be used on the smoker, that are not labeled with the common name of the chemicals. Label all chemicals with the common name of the product. 
7-102.11  (Pf) Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11  (P) Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. Reference 7-204.11.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment: Observed a couple of soy sauce buckets that had white powders in them (salt) that were not labeled with the common name of the product. Make sure to label all foods removed from their original containers with the common name of the product.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12  (C) Food storage containers are not labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: Observed the drain pipe underneath the three compartment sink to have a can underneath it collecting dripping water from the pipe. Repair drip.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15  (C)  Repair plumbing according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.
